text:
Alex G: Heads up — downtown office closed tomorrow for emergency maintenance. My team is mid-sprint and a few folks had PTO planned later this week. Can we swap PTO days or convert to a floating holiday so we can keep coverage? Also, what happens to carryover if we shift dates? TL;DR: fastest ops-approved path?

HR Bot: Automated note — people-ops inbox received this thread. Please allow a few hours. Quick policy link: https://intranet.redwood/hr/pto

Maria S: @Alex G you can submit a 'PTO date change' request via People Portal -> Time off -> Edit. If it's within 72h notice, tag me and we'll expedite. :+1:

Jamal R: If they're swapping with another teammate (shift swap), we usually require an ad hoc agreement + manager signoff. Manager must approve in the portal before we finalize.

Alex G: Any blackout rules this week? trying not to break anything.

Rebecca (People Ops): No org-wide blackout this week — last week's EoQ freeze was the one. For sprint-critical coverage we can approve same-week swaps if managers confirm coverage. Note: contractors have different accrual/eligibility, check contracts.

Maria S: Contractors typically don't follow the employee carryover rules. Some have paid time in contract, others don't — pro-rate applies. Ping legal/eng-ops if unsure.

Jamal R: Can we convert PTO to a floating holiday retroactively? example: someone used PTO but office closure happened.

Rebecca (People Ops): Retro conversions are possible but reserved for exceptional cases (office closures, outages). File a ticket with dates + rationale; we'll review. For full-team closures we generally approve.

Alex G: Good. I'll gather names and manager approvals. What's the quick checklist to include in the ticket so we don't go back and forth?

HR Bot: Suggested ticket body:
1) Employee name(s)
2) Original PTO date(s)
3) Requested new date(s) or 'convert to floating holiday'
4) Manager approval screenshot/text
5) Reason (office closure)
6) Contract type (employee/contractor)

Maria S: Also indicate if the employee prefers carryover instead of swap — carryover follows yearly cap rules (see policy link above).

Jamal R: Thanks — I'll coordinate swaps. One more: if someone wants unpaid leave instead, that's a separate flow, right?

Rebecca (People Ops): Correct. Unpaid leave requires manager + finance approval. Put 'unpaid' in the ticket and cc payroll.

Alex G: Great, will do. Tagging @Rebecca and @Maria to expedite if we push this through. :pray:
